proof_summary: Factorials are split into their p-divisible and reduced-residue parts, expressing adjacent binomial coefficients through block products \(G_c=\prod_{p\nmid t<p^r}(t+cp^r)\); p-adic product expansions, with reciprocal-square sum divisibility and a mod-\(p\) vanishing sum, give \(G_c\equiv G_0\pmod{p^{3r-v_p(3)}}\) and \(G_2G_0^2\equiv G_1^3\pmod{p^{3r+3}}\). Telescoping supplies the needed mod-\(p^3\) base approximations, and an algebraic combination of these estimates cancels the first-order increments while all higher-order terms have sufficient p-adic valuation.
